examples.japanese: 新幹線の中では、東京から青森まで３時間立ちっぱなしだった。足が痛くなっちゃった！
examples.body_text:
新幹線の中では、東京から青森まで３時間立ちっぱなしだった。足が痛くなっちゃった！ 

		On the shinkansen from Toukyou to Aomori I kept standing up for 3 hours. My feet hurt!
examples.body_html:
新幹線の中では、東京から青森まで３時間立ちっぱなしだった。足が痛くなっちゃった！ 
On the shinkansen from Toukyou to Aomori I kept standing up for 3 hours. My feet hurt!

examples.japanese: ここに置きっぱなしにしちゃダメでしょ。
examples.body_text:
ここに置きっぱなしにしちゃダメでしょ。 

		Hey, you can't leave your things here.
examples.body_html:
ここに置きっぱなしにしちゃダメでしょ。 
Hey, you can't leave your things here.

examples.japanese: ゴミを散らかしっぱなしにしないでね。
examples.body_text:
ゴミを散らかしっぱなしにしないでね。 

		Don't drop your 
		 
		rubbish about, ok.
examples.body_html:
ゴミを散らかしっぱなしにしないでね。 
Don't drop your rubbish about, ok.

examples.japanese: 友達のビデオが借りっぱなしだ。早く返さなくちゃ。
examples.body_text:
友達のビデオが借りっぱなしだ。早く返さなくちゃ。 

		I borrowed my friends video and didn't return it.  I'd better return it soon.
examples.body_html:
友達のビデオが借りっぱなしだ。早く返さなくちゃ。 
I borrowed my friends video and didn't return it. I'd better return it soon.

comments.text: This is a rare case of 一級 grammar that I hear in every day conversation.  I learnt this when I was still a beginner.  I think it has a similar meaning to "〜たまま".
comments.html: This is a rare case of 一級 grammar that I hear in every day conversation.  I learnt this when I was still a beginner.  I think it has a similar meaning to "〜たまま".

comments.text: It is a colloqual form of 放し, meaning doing something and leave it at that.It has a lot more emphasis than ...たままにする.

comments.text:
How can I know how must I read the kanji, if in on yomi or kunyomi.

For example: in nﾂｰ 5446 is:

koko ni "TE" ki ppanachi

or

koko ni "OKU" ki ppanachi?

It is very difficult for people who donﾂｴt know japanese very well.
comments.html:
How can I know how must I read the kanji, if in on yomi or kunyomi.
For example: in nﾂｰ 5446 is:
koko ni "TE" ki ppanachi
or
koko ni "OKU" ki ppanachi?
It is very difficult for people who donﾂｴt know japanese very well.

comments.text:
It's not that difficult.

The fact that there's a hiragana 'ki' after it tells you that it should be 'oki'. This has nothing to do with this grammar though...

comments.text: It's common practice that in compounds you'll be using onyomi.
